text_full:
On the subject of making something original (see post #1):

Did you know that custom clothing is cheap and easy to order?

I don’t mean made-to-measure suits and dress shirts — I’m talking about T-shirts and hats. On the site I use, custom shirts cost me around $15-25 total, including shipping:

That's cheaper than a lot of non-custom shirts! It's clearly meant for people running online merch shops, but there's no reason you can't use it for one-offs.

The biggest benefit is that your clothes will be unique: nobody else will have the same shirt as you. Express your individuality without the long-term commitment of a tattoo.

And it's actually better for the environment. Custom items are printed when you order them, and everyone's designs are made with the same base shirts. So there's less waste and no leftover unsold clothes heading to a landfill somewhere.

There are some downsides, too, of course. You can't return things, so you're a bit stuck if the shirt doesn't fit well. And it takes longer for items to ship since they have to be made to order (duh). Also, it's more work — you have to actually think of an idea for a shirt you want to wear and design it!

But to me those tradeoffs are totally worth it. I've practically got my own fashion line these days. I started with custom shirts for my fantasy football franchise (including a recent rebrand):

I've made a couple of items with this little ASCII golfer / "hacker" character:

This one was a gift for someone based on a sign we liked in Austin, TX:

I needed some new base layer shirts, so I ordered a couple with simple little logos I'd doodled at work:

And lastly, "no more 3-putts", which gets a lot of love from fellow golfers who want to know if the shirt's magic works (it doesn't):

Like what you see? Want to buy one of these shirts?

TOO BAD! Make your own! That's the whole point!
